layer: L1-L6 / Rust mapping of surfaces retired by the D797 kernel set
question: How does graphrefly-rs replace the PULL, PAUSE/RESUME, TEARDOWN, Pausable, kernel-only RESOLVED and Python-only host-boundary surfaces that graphrefly:D798/D799/D800 retire, while the pause, demand, history, checkpoint and restart modules stay root drafts?
decision: Without implementing those modules, in graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS: (1) each pull_id holder (data_structures, messaging, work_queue) exposes a request state node in place of its pull_id and declares it as a dependency; a request is a write to it, with paging or limit params in its value, and the work_queue admission pager writes that state instead of sending PULL up. (2) The pause machinery (LockId, the pause lockset and buffer, Pausable and its source settings) is removed. (3) TEARDOWN and its reactors are removed; SyncValueFromError::Teardown goes, and the sync collector ends on COMPLETE or ERROR. (4) worker.rs sends nothing where it sent [RESOLVED]. (5) HostBoundaryAbort (graphrefly:D431, superseded by graphrefly:D800) is removed with host_boundary.rs and its handlers in the dispatcher, boundary drains, rewire drain, subscribe and batch drains, since only the Python binding armed it. (6) In Rust the retired message types are unrepresentable in process; C-26 and C-42 evidence is that the Message enum has no such variant and Ctx and Node have no upward call, that the crate's canonical wire codec (adapters/bridge_protobuf.rs) carries no Message or Wave, so no retired type can arrive from a peer (its WireEdgeKind DIRTY is renamed PENDING in names only, number 1 unchanged, as spec/protocol.proto does, with the issue codes and status counter named after it; the user chose on 2026-11-10 to do this in phase 1), and that ctx.down, DeferredCtx::down and Node::down reject START, PENDING and RESOLVED at run time (START since graphrefly:D801). (7) The existing checkpoint.rs is changed only where the kernel changes force it and makes no R-checkpoint claim. (8) Host-level Node::replace_deps, subscribe_dep and unsubscribe_dep callers are decided per call site at the start of phase 5. No compatibility path is kept.
rationale: graphrefly:D797 leaves no upward channel and no control message; control is data on a declared edge. A read-only inventory (2026-11-10) found that no production code originates PAUSE, RESUME or TEARDOWN, that the only upward sender is the work_queue admission pager's PULL, that the only non-core RESOLVED sender is worker.rs, and that only crates/graphrefly-bindings-py arms HostBoundaryAbort. The user chose these mappings on 2026-11-10, following graphrefly-ts:D172 where the surfaces match. Corrected the same day before any commit: the first wording said the wire decoder rejects message numbers 8 to 11, but the Rust codec encodes only bridge envelopes and wire-edge frames and has no message decoder.

completion.complete_when: graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS lands these replacements with focused tests and the phase gates pass.
completion.historical_when: A Rust pause, demand, checkpoint or restart module is admitted and replaces the matching mapping.

layer: L1-L6 / Rust host input surface under the D797 kernel set
question: What is the Rust public surface for host input and subscription under graphrefly:D797 (R-wave@2: a wave starts from a host input to a state node), aligned with the TypeScript and Python packages?
decision: (1) Host input exists only on a state handle: Graph::state, Node::state and their empty forms return State<T>, whose set(w), invalidate(), complete() and error(e) are the only host inputs; State<T> gives its Node<T> for subscribing and as a dependency. (2) Node<T> and GraphNode have no public host write: Node::down, GraphNode::down and Node::set are removed; raw arrays leave a node only through ctx.down and DeferredCtx::down. Graph has no host input of its own. (3) A subscriber's sink is Fn(&[Message<AnyValue>]) and is called once per array with the whole array, the START array included. (4) One set writes a value or a function of the value, as R-request-order's set(id, value | fn) does: set(w: impl Into<StateWrite<T>>), where StateWrite<T> is Value(T) or Function(f) with f: FnOnce(Option<&T>) -> Option<T>. A plain value converts by From<T>, so s.set(5) writes 5, always, an equal value included. A function is given as StateWrite::from_fn(f): f receives the state's value when the write runs in request order (None when it has none, as after INVALIDATE), and returning None writes nothing, the Rust form of 'a function that returns the value it was given writes nothing'; Some(v) writes v. Rust has no overloading, and one trait accepting both a value and a closure would overlap for T that is itself a closure, so the function form is a variant of set's argument rather than a second method; a value of a closure type is therefore written as a value, which is the rule's 'a function is written as a value only wrapped in another' turned around: here a function is applied only when wrapped. TypeScript and Python fold the function form into set the same way (the user, 2026-11-10). (5) Timing in graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS: (1) to (3) in phase 2, the function form of set in phase 5. No compatibility path is kept.
rationale: R-wave@2 starts a wave only from a host input to a state node, a batch commit, a function's output or a topology snapshot, so a public down or set on any node is a host input the rules do not have. The user chose, in the cross-runtime alignment session on 2026-11-10, one shared host-input surface for TS, Rust and Python and, for Rust, the Option-returning update recommended by the Rust owner over an Rc identity comparison, since the rule asks only that a function can say 'write nothing' and an explicit None avoids Rc identity in user code. Revised the same day before its commit, after the user folded update into set for every runtime (D797's own wording, missed in the first alignment): the Option-returning function stays, as the function variant of set's argument.

completion.complete_when: graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS phases 2 and 5 land this surface with focused tests.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the host input or subscription surface.

layer: L4 / Rust checkpoint stage under graphrefly:D802
question: Does graphrefly-rs:D797-KERNEL-MIGRATION-RS take up the checkpoint module that graphrefly:D802 activated, and what replaces graphrefly-rs:D1 (7)?
decision: Yes. A checkpoint stage follows phase 5 (it builds on setup, replace, ctx.rewire and definition) and brings crates/graphrefly's checkpoint to R-checkpoint@1, as the root handoff's 'Checkpoint after D802' section lists: capture only at a wave boundary (refused inside a wave and inside an open batch body); a restored graph has no subscribers and a restored node receives no waves before its first activation; each node's received inputs per dependency are saved, and at the first activation the function runs once on only the changed dependencies, keeping the saved value otherwise; the setup runs at the restored first activation; recipe and setup belong to the instance, and a replace without a recipe makes the node local-only; each node is built after its declared dependencies and a ctx.rewire's lifetime dependencies are saved; an ended node comes back ended with its dependencies and without private state, with an ERROR payload saved as JSON; the D109 version field and its restore checks leave the checkpoint, and a checkpoint lacking what the rule saves is refused at restore. The layout beyond JSON, its version tag and existing checkpoints are Rust's: the layout changes, its format tag is bumped and older checkpoints are refused. This replaces graphrefly-rs:D1 (7), under which checkpoint.rs changed only where the kernel forced it and made no R-checkpoint claim. C-38 is qualified at the end of the stage; C-45 and C-46 wait for their modules.
rationale: graphrefly:D802 activated R-checkpoint@1 on 2026-11-10 and the user asked earlier that TS and Rust implement checkpoint too; the alignment session relayed the admission, and the user confirmed the continuous plan in this session ('是，按新做法').

completion.complete_when: The checkpoint stage lands with C-38 qualified and the gates pass.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the checkpoint layout or scope.

layer: L2 / Rust host reporter under R-failure@3 and R-graph-domain@2
question: Where does a failure with no caller and no node to end go in the Rust runtime, and what is the host reporter's Rust shape?
decision: A panic from a user sink (Node::subscribe, graph observe), a lifetime cleanup or release, or a queued request is caught; the fanout or close goes on, no node ends for it, and the failure goes to the host reporter of the domain it happened in. The reporter is the graph's option, as the reference's createGraph({ report }) and Python's Graph(report=...): GraphOptions.report: Option<HostReporter> (GraphOptions::with_report(f)), where HostReporter = Rc<dyn Fn(&HostFailure)> and HostFailure { source, error }; sources are "sink", "cleanup", "release" and "queued request". The reporter lives on the graph's arena, so a mounted graph keeps its own. A queued request carries the reporter of the graph it was made for; a batch commit spanning graphs reports to its first staged target's graph. Nodes built outside any Graph (Node::state, Node::derived and the like) live in the default domain, which has no reporter: their failures are dropped. Without a reporter nothing is kept; a reporter that panics is ignored. Dependency edges are kernel edges and are not guarded. Revised 2026-11-10 at the alignment session's request: the first version used a per-thread graphrefly::set_host_reporter, which is removed.
rationale: R-failure@3 sends any failure that is not a function's throw or an invalid output to its caller or, with none, to a host reporter callback, and never into an unrelated node; R-graph-domain@2 makes the graph the concurrency domain, and the reference and Python take the reporter where the graph is built. A per-thread setter would be hidden global state and split the shape from the other runtimes.

completion.complete_when: The graph-option reporter lands with C-33, C-34 and C-28's reporter clauses and host_reporter_is_the_graph_option passing.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the reporter's shape.

layer: L2 / Rust lifetime and status shapes under R-lifetime@2 and R-node
question: What Rust shapes carry the setup, cleanup, abort signal and derived status, and what happens to Ctx::on_deactivation, Ctx::on_invalidate and Ctx::state_persist?
decision: The setup is node option NodeOpts.setup: Option<Setup> (NodeOpts::with_setup(f)), where f: Fn(&Ctx) -> Option<Cleanup> and Cleanup = Box<dyn FnOnce(&CleanupCtx)>; CleanupCtx::state_get reads the closing lifetime's private state, which is dropped after the cleanup returns. graphrefly::cleanup(f) wraps a closure as Some(Cleanup). Ctx::signal() and DeferredCtx::signal() give the lifetime's AbortSignal (is_aborted). Ctx and DeferredCtx are bound to their lifetime: emit, down, state_set and the rewire_next_* requests through a closed lifetime's ctx are dropped, and state_get returns None. Ctx::on_deactivation, Ctx::on_invalidate and Ctx::state_persist are removed with no replacement shim: private state lasts exactly one lifetime, manual INVALIDATE replaces on_invalidate, and each production caller opens its resource in a setup (sources through a crate-private source_op whose setup runs the source body; Graph::effect and worker_derived keep their latest per-run cleanup in private state and their setup's cleanup runs it). A cleanup's or a release's panic goes to the host reporter (graphrefly-rs:D6) as source "cleanup" or "release". Node::status() returns Status { cache: CacheStatus (Empty, Stale, Ready), output: OutputStatus (Open, Completed, Errored), lifecycle: Lifecycle (Inactive, Active, Closing) }, computed from what the node holds and never stored; Status::label() gives empty, stale, ready, completed or errored, which describe, render and the checkpoint's status field use until the checkpoint stage (graphrefly-rs:D5) changes that layout; the checkpoint's ctxState.persist field is removed.
rationale: R-lifetime@2 has the setup belong to the instance and return the cleanup, the cleanup read private state before it is dropped, a closed lifetime's ctx drop its output and requests, and no function register cleanup; R-node derives status from three facets. The reference kernel takes the setup as a node option, so Rust does too. A cleanup gets a CleanupCtx rather than capturing the ctx because a Rust ctx is borrowed for one invocation and a captured node handle would keep the node alive. The aggregates that used state_persist (CQRS, process, throttle) keep their state for the lifetime; an active node's private state is still captured by the checkpoint.

completion.complete_when: Phase 4 lands with C-4 and the lifetime clauses of C-33 and C-34 qualified.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the setup, cleanup or status shape.

layer: L2 / Rust request queue, replace, ctx.rewire and host-level rewire call sites under R-request-order@2
question: What Rust shapes carry the request queue, replace, definition and ctx.rewire, and what replaces the host-level Node::replace_deps, subscribe_dep and unsubscribe_dep at each production call site?
decision: Requests (host State writes including StateWrite::from_fn, output through a kept DeferredCtx, public subscribe and unsubscribe, replace, ctx.rewire and a batch commit) made during a wave or inside a batch body go to one per-thread FIFO; the outermost wave owner runs them in order after the wave, each as its own wave, and a queued request's panic goes to the host reporter as "queued request". The synchronous-feedback-cycle panic is gone (a debug invariant remains). A batch body's requests run after its commit, before the commit wave's own requests; a commit during a wave is itself a request; a panicking body or write function drops its requests and commits nothing, while the body's topology requests still run after a failed write function. Node::replace(deps, f, ReplaceOpts { setup, recipe }) is a request giving a computed node a new instance (refused for a state node, a duplicate, another graph's node, the node itself or a node that depends on it through current or declared dependencies); subscribers receive START and the new snapshot. Node::definition() returns NodeDefinition { deps (declared), function (the current instance's NodeFn, None for a state), setup, recipe, complete, error, invalidate, quiet }; NodeOpts.recipe holds the creation recipe (an opaque serde_json::Value). Ctx::rewire(deps) and DeferredCtx::rewire(deps) change the node's dependencies for the lifetime, as a request dropped if the lifetime has closed; the declared dependencies come back when it closes; higher_order and time use crate-private rewire_add and rewire_remove, which compute the list when the request runs. Ctx::rewire_next_* and the host-level Node::replace_deps, subscribe_dep and unsubscribe_dep are removed. Call sites: the process command input, the message bus commands input and the wire bridge command and inbound inputs become computed inputs with no declared dependency that rewire themselves to the attached sources through the ctx their setup keeps (crate-private fan_in::FanInSources; kept sources keep their records, so an attach delivers only the added source's snapshot and edges are visible while the input is active); the bridge's command and inbound are therefore computed nodes its own methods write into, as process.command already was; the reactive list and log bind disposers detach their source with a replace to no dependencies. Rust has no async batch body: batch takes a synchronous closure, so C-29's async and promise clauses do not apply. Concurrency domain (revised 2026-11-11 under graphrefly:D803, R-graph-domain@3): each graph's arena owns its domain, holding its own wave scope, delivery scope, request queue and batch frame, so graphs on one thread share none of them: a request to graph B made during graph A's wave runs at once if B is idle, and a write to B inside A's batch body is B's own request, not part of A's commit (C-47). The wave and delivery id counters and the default dispatcher stay per thread (a dispatcher's function table and worker pools may be shared). Nodes built outside any Graph live in the default arena, one per thread, which is their domain; graphrefly::batch is that domain's batch and Graph::batch a graph's. The deviation recorded here on 2026-11-10 is retired. Revised 2026-11-11 (D797 migration review F 2.3, 2.4, 2.9, 2.16; C F5, F12): output through a kept ctx during a wave and a quiet node's output (its auto ERROR included) are requests of that lifetime, dropped if it has closed when they run, in the one FIFO (the committed-boundary queue is gone); a queued replace checks its dependencies again when it runs; a queued host write to an ended node is refused and reported, before a write function runs; describe gives each node's kind (state or node) and whether it is quiet.
rationale: R-request-order@2 makes every in-wave request wait and run in order, puts a batch's requests after its commit, and removes graph-level rewire in favour of replace and a lifetime-scoped ctx.rewire. The fan-in inputs keep today's behaviour of the removed replace_deps (kept sources keep their records; an added source delivers its snapshot) and their visible describe edges; a replace would rerun every kept source's snapshot and could dispatch a retained command twice. DeferredCtx::rewire is the kept-ctx form the reference kernel's ctx.rewire allows after the run.

completion.complete_when: Phase 5 lands with C-6, C-11, C-29, C-33, C-34, C-35, C-37, the replace clause of C-40 and the rest of C-28 qualified.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes these shapes or call-site choices.

layer: L2 / Rust checkpoint layout and restore under R-checkpoint@1
question: What layout and restore behaviour does the Rust checkpoint take for R-checkpoint@1 (graphrefly:D802), and what happens to the D109 version field, D160 backendState and existing checkpoints?
decision: The layout tag becomes graphrefly.checkpoint.v2 and earlier checkpoints are refused at restore. Each node saves id, name, its current instance's recipe as factory (a registry reference with JSON config, read from NodeOpts.recipe or ReplaceOpts.recipe; GraphNodeOpts.restore is copied into the recipe when the graph registers the node; a state registered as "state" falls back to the state reference; anything else without a recipe is local-only), declared deps, lifetimeDeps when a ctx.rewire changed them, the values of its last array, its terminal with the ERROR payload saved as a JSON string, and, for a computed node with a lifetime (or an unconsumed seed), privateState and received (per current dependency: the values of its last array and its terminal); a computed node without a lifetime that has not ended holds nothing. status, lifecycle, ctxState and the D109 version field leave the checkpoint, with their restore checks and the now-unused versioning helpers; node runtime versioning itself stays. Capture is refused inside a wave and inside a batch body; every saved value, private state and recipe configuration must be JSON. Restore builds each node after its declared dependencies and otherwise in checkpoint order, runs no recipe function and gives each node a seed: a state its values and terminal; an ended computed node its values and terminal; any other computed node with a received record a seed its first activation consumes (its lifetime dependencies, private state and received records): its setup runs, and its function runs once with only the dependencies whose values or terminal changed (an end alone without the values) and otherwise does not run; a replace drops the seed. A collection's backend is saved as its delta node's privateState (a collection is a node whose backend is its private state); the separate backendState field is gone. The collections (reactive list, log, map, index) still keep the backend at run time in a store the collection API writes directly, outside the node's function, so the fold is at the checkpoint layout, not in how the node holds its state. GraphNode::as_node::<T>() gives a found node's typed handle, and DeferredCtx::state_get and state_set give a kept ctx the lifetime's private state. Ctx::seed::<S>() gives the seed's note on the seeded instance's first run and None on every other run (R-invocation@2); a restored node's note is its received records as JSON. A checkpoint is refused for a computed node saved with a lifetime (private state, lifetime dependencies, or values while it has not ended) but without its received record (revised 2026-11-11, D797 migration review F 2.7, C F8). Restored values and private state are serde_json::Value whatever Rust type the saved graph used: the checkpoint carries JSON and restore runs no recipe that could decode it, so a restored node is read as Value (as_node::<serde_json::Value>()), and a graph meant to round-trip is written over Value (review F 2.18; recorded in the checkpoint module docs).
rationale: R-checkpoint@1 and the root handoff's 'Checkpoint after D802' list fix what is saved and how a restored node starts; the layout beyond JSON, its version tag and what to do with older checkpoints are the package's. The ERROR payload in Rust is the error's message (DepTerminal keeps the message), so it is always JSON. A Rust process or CQRS bundle over typed values retains non-JSON values and is refused at capture, as the rule requires; tests/process.rs checks that refusal.

completion.complete_when: The checkpoint stage lands with C-38 qualified and the gates pass.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the checkpoint layout.

layer: L2 / Rust wire edge groups and the envelope bridge's inputs under R-bridge@2
question: What Rust shape do the wire edge groups and the envelope bridge's command and inbound inputs take under graphrefly:D803 and D804 (R-bridge@2)?
decision: Wire edge groups follow the reference module's public shape in Rust casing (crate::adapters::wire_edge_group): wire_edge_group_out(graph, name, group, edges: Vec<(String, Core)>) -> Node<WireEdgeCause>, frame_sink(send), frame_source(graph, name, open), wire_edge_group_in(graph, name, group, &frames, &[edge]) -> WireEdgeGroupIn { gate, inbound: BTreeMap<String, Node<Vec<u8>>>, issues: Node<WireEdgeIssue> }. WireEdgeCause is the codec's CanonicalWireEdgeCause { group, session, cause, edges: [CanonicalWireEdgeArrays { edge_id, arrays: [[CanonicalWireMessage]] }] }, where CanonicalWireMessage has only DATA(bytes), INVALIDATE, COMPLETE and ERROR(bytes), so a frame carrying PENDING, RESOLVED or START cannot be built in Rust and the codec refuses such bytes as invalid_wire_edge. DATA values must be Vec<u8>; any other value panics in the outbound node (its ERROR). An ERROR's payload is its message's UTF-8 bytes, and the receiving inbound node's ERROR carries that text. A session id is made by the outbound node's setup from the node name, the time and a counter. The gate's issues are WireEdgeIssue values (Malformed, Stale, Gap, Refused). The old wire_edge_group bundle with per-edge PENDING/DATA frames, cohorts, tombstones, the release drain and the status node is removed with no shim. The codec encodes and decodes WireEdgeCause (encode/decode_canonical_wire_edge_cause); WireBridgeDataPayload.edge_cause is field 3 and field 2 is refused as an unknown field. The envelope bridge's command and inbound inputs are states again (FanInSources is gone for them, as are attach_/detach_*_source_for_native): the bundle's methods and the host write them, and the remote responder writes its response commands into the bridge's command state from a sink, so there is no describe edge from responseCommands to the command. Under R-bridge@2 (graphrefly:D804, 2026-11-11): an ended inbound node takes nothing more: a later frame's arrays for its edge are skipped and the rest of the frame is released; the skip is reported as WireEdgeIssue::Ended { session, cause, edge } only when the skipped arrays do not end with a terminal, so a new session repeating an ended edge's snapshot and terminal is not reported; refusal of the whole frame stays for an undeclared edge, an edge twice, an empty array, a terminal not last and an array after a terminal in the same frame. The first cause puts an INVALIDATE ahead of the snapshot of every edge without a value, one whose snapshot is its terminal alone included. Revised 2026-11-11 (D797 migration review F 2.13): WireBridgeInbound has no raw array input; its one host write is set(envelope), a typed write to the inbound state.
rationale: R-bridge@1 and the root handoff's 'Bridge after D803' section fix the frame, the gate and the removals; the reference module's names are the public shape. The fixtures (wire_edge_cause.v1.jsonl and the rewritten envelope vectors) all decode, validate and re-encode byte-equal with the Rust codec, so nothing is reported to the root.

completion.complete_when: Phase 6 lands with C-1, C-1a, C-1b (R-bridge@2 clauses included) and C-47 qualified.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes the bridge shape.

layer: L2 / Rust shapes for the D797 migration review's decisions (Q1-Q15)
question: What Rust shapes carry the user's answers to the D797 migration review questions (all as recommended, relayed by the alignment session on 2026-11-11)?
decision: Q3: a function reads each dependency through one view: Ctx::dep(i) returns DepView { id, is(core), raw_waves, waves::<T>, values::<T>, value::<T>, has, terminal, invalidated } and Ctx::deps() iterates them (DeferredCtx::dep the same); an index past the dependencies panics. Ctx::data, batch, batches, wave_data, terminal, invalidated and dep_is are removed. NodeIdentity (the node's arena, slot and generation) is public so DepView::id can name a dependency; nodes that rewire themselves read through a crate-private dep_if(i). Q1: the kernel has no first-run gate: a lifetime's first run happens on activation whatever the dependencies hold, and every later settlement with input runs the function. NodeOpts.partial, the kernel's all-settled check and the per-node has_called_fn_once run slot are removed. Graph::derived and Graph::effect (and their group forms) carry the gate as sugar, as Python's facade does: the callback runs once every dependency has a value, then when a dependency sent DATA in the run; a value sent while the gate waits is kept as the dependency's latest. Values::value(i) reads a dependency's latest value. Q4: Ctx::emit(v) sends one array of its own (it is ctx.down([DATA v])) and Ctx::emit_all(values) sends one array of all of them (nothing when empty); consecutive emits are no longer joined, and the node's open-emit flag is gone. Operators that produce several values in one run from a loop over their input (tap, settle, rescue, valve, take_until, race, zip, buffer_count, concat, fan-in, the collections' projections and the bundles' fact loops) now collect them and send one array with emit_all, so what each sends is unchanged; operators that iterate their input arrays (map, filter, merge, concat's second phase) send one array per input array. Facts a bundle emits through separate helper calls in one run are now separate arrays; downstream nodes read every value either way. Q2: every node belongs to a Graph. Node::state, state_empty, producer, producer_async, producer_opts, derived, derived_async and derived_opts, the free operators::init_node, the per-thread default arena and its domain, and the free graphrefly::batch are removed; a node is built by its graph (Graph::state, node, producer, derived, effect, init_node and the group forms) and a batch is Graph::batch, whose BatchCtx stays as its rollback handle. The collections take the graph as a required first argument (reactive_list, reactive_log, reactive_map, reactive_index, the restore_ and open_persistent_ forms, merge_reactive_logs), their options lose the graph field, and their derived views (tail, slice, scan, merge) are registered in that graph. The one exception is test-only: crate-private arena constructors under cfg(test) let the kernel's own unit tests count handles and arena slots, which a graph's registry would hold; no shipped code can build a node outside a graph. Tests that called the free batch on graph nodes were batching nothing (each graph has its own domain since D803) and now use Graph::batch. Q7: D109 node versioning is removed: src/versioning.rs (NodeVersion, NodeVersioningPolicy, the V0/V1 hash and its default), NodeOpts.versioning, GraphOptions.versioning, the per-node version slot, Node::version, GraphNode::version and DescribeNode.version. The wire bridge's admission never read a node version (R-bridge@2 admits by cause, graphrefly:D804), so no private counter replaces it.
rationale: R-ctx names ctx.deps[i] as a view; both reviewers found three packages with three shapes, and the user chose the rule's own shape (Q3). One API also removes the parallel index methods TS and Rust had grown.

completion.complete_when: Every review B item (Q1-Q5, Q7, Q9, Q12, Q13, Q15) has landed on d797-kernel-migration with evidence.
completion.historical_when: A later Rust decision changes these shapes.
